h: Pheochromocytoma (episodic headache, palpitations): first drug before surgery?
p: Start an alpha blocker first; unopposed beta blockade can cause a hypertensive crisis. Family history of medullary thyroid cancer and hyperparathyroidism suggests MEN2.

h: Peanut aspiration while lying supine: most affected lung segment?
a: Superior segment of right lower lobe
d: Anterior segment of right upper lobe
Inferior segment of left lower lobe
p: Supine aspiration favors the superior segment of the right lower lobe (and posterior right upper lobe); upright aspiration favors the basal right lower lobe. The right main bronchus is wider and straighter.

h: CAH with hypertension and virilization: deficient enzyme?
p: 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency raises 11-deoxycorticosterone (a mineralocorticoid: hypertension, low renin) and androgens (virilization). 21-hydroxylase causes salt wasting; 17-alpha-hydroxylase causes hypertension with ambiguous genitalia in males.

h: Osteomalacia (vitamin D deficiency): which process is impaired?
p: Without vitamin D, osteoid forms but fails to mineralize, giving bone pain, proximal weakness and Looser zones; rickets in children.

h: Early diastolic murmur at left sternal border: expected pulse finding?
p: Aortic regurgitation causes wide pulse pressure, bounding (water hammer) pulses and an early decrescendo diastolic murmur; pulsus parvus et tardus is aortic stenosis.

h: Calcineurin inhibitor (blocks IL-2 transcription): main toxicity?
p: Cyclosporine and tacrolimus cause nephrotoxicity, hypertension, tremor and hyperglycemia (tacrolimus). Pancytopenia is more typical of azathioprine or mycophenolate.

h: Earlier expanding rash, then recurrent knee arthritis, negative Gram stain: organism?
p: Late Lyme disease causes recurrent oligoarthritis, usually the knee, months after erythema migrans; treat with doxycycline or amoxicillin.

h: Listeria infection in pregnancy: transmission source?
p: Listeria monocytogenes (cold-growing, tumbling motility) is foodborne from soft cheeses and deli meats; causes neonatal sepsis and meningitis. Treat with ampicillin.

h: Hypoglycemia after exogenous insulin overdose: C-peptide?
a: Low or absent C-peptide with high insulin
p: Exogenous insulin lacks C-peptide and suppresses endogenous secretion; insulinoma and sulfonylurea overdose raise both insulin and C-peptide.

h: Restrictive pattern (FEV1/FVC 90%), dry cough, late inspiratory crackles: biopsy finding?
p: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: usual interstitial pneumonia with basal subpleural fibrosis, honeycomb cysts and clubbing; nintedanib or pirfenidone slow decline.

h: Dorsal column and spinocerebellar degeneration with hemolytic anemia: deficient vitamin?
p: Vitamin E is an antioxidant; deficiency causes hemolysis, ataxia and posterior column loss, seen in fat malabsorption (cystic fibrosis, abetalipoproteinemia).

h: Child with ataxia, downward-fixed eyes (setting sun), nystagmus: mass in which structure?
p: Pineal tumors (germinoma) compress the dorsal midbrain, causing Parinaud syndrome (upgaze palsy, light-near dissociation) and obstructive hydrocephalus.

h: School-age child defiant toward authority, no violation of others' rights: diagnosis?
p: ODD: at least 6 months of negativistic, hostile, defiant behavior toward authority without serious violations of others' rights, unlike conduct disorder.

h: Physical sunscreen protecting against UVA photoaging?
p: Zinc oxide and titanium dioxide are broad-spectrum physical blockers (UVA and UVB). Salicylates mainly absorb UVB.

h: Athlete collapses during exertion and recovers: expected cardiac finding?
p: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the leading cause of sudden death in young athletes: outflow obstruction, harsh systolic murmur louder with Valsalva, autosomal dominant sarcomere mutations.

h: Diuretic causing hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia, hypercalcemia: mechanism?
a: NCC inhibition in the distal convoluted tubule (thiazide)
d: NKCC inhibition in the loop of Henle
ENaC inhibition in the collecting duct
p: Thiazides block the Na+/Cl- cotransporter, spare calcium (hypercalcemia), and can cause hyponatremia, hyperlipidemia and gout; loop diuretics cause hypocalcemia.

h: Swimmer's ear (acute otitis externa): classic organism?
p: Water exposure macerates the canal; Pseudomonas is the most common cause. Malignant otitis externa in diabetics is also Pseudomonas and can invade skull base.

h: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes occurs in which phase?
p: Recombination (chiasmata) occurs in prophase I of meiosis, generating genetic diversity.

h: Adolescent athlete with sore swollen tibial tuberosities: diagnosis?
p: Traction apophysitis of the patellar tendon insertion from repetitive quadriceps pull; self-limited with rest and activity modification.

h: Enteropeptidase activates trypsinogen by which mechanism?
p: Brush-border enteropeptidase removes a hexapeptide from trypsinogen; trypsin then activates other pancreatic zymogens (chymotrypsinogen, proelastase, procarboxypeptidase).

h: Woman of reproductive age with acute RLQ pain: first test?
p: Exclude ectopic pregnancy before further workup in any woman of childbearing age with abdominal pain; ruptured ectopic is life-threatening.
